==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*mey- (change)}}
At least by 1422, from late {{inh|en|enm|omitten}}, borrowed from {{der|en|la|omittō||to let go}}, from {{m|la|ob-}} + {{m|la|mittō||to send}}, but also had the connotations “to fail to perform” and “to neglect”.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/əʊˈmɪt/|/əˈmɪt/|a=UK}}
* {{IPA|en|/oʊˈmɪt/|/əˈmɪt/|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-omit.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪt|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb|++}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[leave out]] or [[exclude]].
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[fail]] to [[perform]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1988|author=w:Douglas Adams|title=w:The Long Dark Tea-Time of the Soul|publisher=William Heinemann Ltd|page=136|passage=She climbed out of the car and carefully '''omitted''' to lock it. She never left anything of value in it, and she found that it was to her advantage if people didn’t have to break anything in order to find that out.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|law|of text}} To [[delete]] or [[remove]]; to [[strike]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|rare}} To [[neglect]] or [[take no notice of]].

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|leave out or exclude}} {{l|en|leave off}}, {{l|en|miss out}}; see also [[Thesaurus:omit]]
* {{sense|fail to perform}}
* {{sense|take no notice of}} {{l|en|disregard}}, {{l|en|ignore}}, {{l|en|pass}}, {{l|en|turn a blind eye}}

====Derived terms====
{{col|en|omittability|omittable|omittance|omitter|unomitted}}

====Related terms====
* {{l|en|omission}}
* {{l|en|mission}}
* {{l|en|elide}}
